claims.claim: Full-length Bid can localize to the mitochondria.
claims.source: Interestingly, full-length Bid can also localize to the mitochondria (Maryanovich et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Bid-/- MPCs display decreased growth rates due to decreased viability, not altered proliferation.
claims.source: Consistent with a pro-survival function, Bid-/- myeloid progenitor cells (MPCs) display decreased growth rates not due to altered proliferation, but instead as a result of decreased viability (p<0.05) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Mitochondria in Bid-/- MPCs are highly abnormal compared to Bid +/+ MPCs.
claims.source: Compared to Bid +/+ MPCs, mitochondria in Bid-/- MPCs were highly abnormal.
claims.evidence: This is supported by TEM images shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Bid-/- MPCs have a significant decrease in the number of cristae compared to Bid +/+ MPCs.
claims.source: Quantitation of the average number of cristae per mitochondrion revealed a significant decrease in the number of cristae in Bid-/- MPCs compared to Bid +/+ MPCs (p<0.0001) (Figure 2c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2c.

claims.claim: Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing FHA-BidBH3 can rescue cristae structure.
claims.source: This function is independent of Bid's apoptotic role, as Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing Flag-HA-tagged full-length Bid mutated in either in its BH3-domain (FHA-BidBH3) or caspase-8 cleavage site D59 (FHA-BidD59A) could rescue cristae structure (p<0.0001) (Figure 2c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2c.

claims.claim: Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing FHA-BidD59A can rescue cristae structure.
claims.source: This function is independent of Bid's apoptotic role, as Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing Flag-HA-tagged full-length Bid mutated in either in its BH3-domain (FHA-BidBH3) or caspase-8 cleavage site D59 (FHA-BidD59A) could rescue cristae structure (p<0.0001) (Figure 2c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 2c.

claims.claim: Bid's cristae regulation function is independent of Bid's apoptotic role.
claims.source: This function is independent of Bid's apoptotic role, as Bid-/- MPCs stably expressing Flag-HA-tagged full-length Bid mutated in either in its BH3-domain (FHA-BidBH3) or caspase-8 cleavage site D59 (FHA-BidD59A) could rescue cristae structure (p<0.0001) (Figure 2c).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the ability of BH3 and D59A mutants to rescue cristae structure.

claims.claim: Bid-/- cells have a slight decrease in mitochondrial density per cell compared to Bid+/+ cells.
claims.source: Furthermore, quantitation of the area density of mitochondria per cell revealed a slight decrease in density in the Bid-/- cells compared to Bid+/+ cells (p<0.05), while FHA-BidD59A expressing cells had increased mitochondrial density compared to all other cell lines (Figure 2d).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claims.claim: FHA-BidD59A expressing cells have increased mitochondrial density compared to all other cell lines.
claims.source: Furthermore, quantitation of the area density of mitochondria per cell revealed a slight decrease in density in the Bid-/- cells compared to Bid+/+ cells (p<0.05), while FHA-BidD59A expressing cells had increased mitochondrial density compared to all other cell lines (Figure 2d).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claims.claim: Overexpression of full-length WT Bid but not FHA-BidBH3 or FHA-BidD59A results in the production of endogenous cBid in the absence of a death stimulus.
claims.source: Indeed, overexpression of full-length WT Bid (Bid-/- + FHA Bid) but not FHA-BidBH3 or FHA-BidD59A results in the production of endogenous cBid in the absence of a death stimulus (Figure 2e).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2e.

claims.claim: In a myeloid cell line, Bid's apoptotic domains must be mutated to fully restore cristae.
claims.source: Thus, in a myeloid cell line, we observe that Bid's apoptotic domains must be mutated to fully restore cristae.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that WT Bid produces cBid and fails to rescue cristae, while BH3 and D59A mutants succeed.

claims.claim: Loss of Bid does not lead to compensatory upregulation of Bim, Bad, or Puma in MPCs or LV cardiac tissue.
claims.source: We evaluated Bid-/- cellular extracts as well as lysate from left ventricular (LV) cardiac tissue which are highly enriched in mitochondria, and find no compensatory upregulation of Bim, Bad, or Puma to account for the observed loss of cristae structure in Bid-/- cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b and c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b and c.

claims.claim: Full-length Bid is found in a heavy membrane, mitochondrial-enriched fraction absent of cytosolic contamination.
claims.source: We find full-length Bid in a heavy membrane, mitochondrial-enriched fraction absent of cytosolic contamination (Figure 3a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by subcellular fractionation data shown in Figure 3a.

claims.claim: Full-length Bid is observed in mitochondria isolated from liver tissue, both in a crude mitochondrial fraction and in a Percoll purified fraction.
claims.source: We also observe full-length Bid in mitochondria isolated from liver tissue, both in a crude mitochondrial fraction as well as in a Percoll purified fraction (Figure 3b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3b.

claims.claim: A pool of Bid remains uncleaved with Proteinase K treatment under conditions in which Bak is cleaved.
claims.source: We observe that a pool of Bid remains uncleaved with PK, under conditions in which we observe cleaved Bak (Figure 3c), a protein associated with the OMM.
claims.evidence: This is supported by Proteinase K treatment data shown in Figure 3c.

claims.claim: Bid is enriched in the mitoplast-containing fraction compared to the OMM.
claims.source: We find an enrichment of Bid in the mitoplast-containing fraction compared to the OMM (Figure 3d).
claims.evidence: This is supported by mitochondrial subfractionation data shown in Figure 3d.

claims.claim: Full-length Bid can localize to the mitochondria during non-apoptotic conditions and is found both at the OMM as well as in the mitoplast.
claims.source: Taken together, the above results suggest that full-length Bid can localize to the mitochondria during non-apoptotic conditions and is found both at the OMM as well as in the mitoplast.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the fractionation and Proteinase K experiments.

claims.claim: Mitochondria cristae defects in humans can result in severe abnormalities in multiple organ systems, especially the heart.
claims.source: Mitochondria cristae defects in humans can result in severe abnormalities in multiple organ systems, especially the heart (Brown et al., 2017; Meyers et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Left ventricular tissue isolated from Bid-/- mice reveals striking irregularities both in gross mitochondrial organization between myofibrils as well as loss of normal lamellar cristae structure.
claims.source: TEM of left ventricular tissue isolated from Bid-/- mice revealed striking irregularities both in gross mitochondrial organization between myofibrils as well as loss of normal lamellar cristae structure (Figure 4a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TEM images shown in Figure 4a.

claims.claim: Without treatment, Bid-/- tissue has overall decreased mitochondrial electron density corresponding to significantly increased cristae width.
claims.source: Specifically, without treatment, Bid-/- tissue had overall decreased mitochondrial electron density corresponding to significantly increased cristae width (p<0.0001) (Figure 4b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of TEM images shown in Figure 4b.

claims.claim: 18 hours after 0.5 mg/kg Epinephrine treatment, both Bid+/+ and Bid-/- tissues are damaged, but the Bid-/- cristae are significantly more deformed.
claims.source: We assessed both Bid+/+ and Bid-/- mitochondria 18 hr after a dose of 0.5 mg/kg Epi and find that while both Bid+/+ and Bid-/- tissues are damaged, the Bid-/- cristae are significantly more deformed (p<0.0001) (Figure 4a and b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TEM images and quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4a and b.

claims.claim: Damaged cristae in Bid-/- mice after Epinephrine treatment are structurally similar to mitochondria observed after induction of an acute myocardial infarction.
claims.source: Interestingly, these damaged cristae are structurally similar to mitochondria observed after induction of an acute myocardial infarction (MI) (Bryant et al., 1958).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature describing MI-induced mitochondrial damage.

claims.claim: Bid-/- mice have a severe cardiac cristae defect that results in increased susceptibility to acute stress-induced damage.
claims.source: Thus, Bid-/- mice have a severe cardiac cristae defect that results in increased susceptibility to acute stress-induced damage.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the TEM data showing increased cristae damage in Bid-/- mice after Epinephrine treatment.

claims.claim: Cardiac function does not differ between Bid+/+ and Bid-/- mice at baseline.
claims.source: Cardiac function does not differ at baseline.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by echocardiography data in Figure 4.

claims.claim: 18 hours after acute Epinephrine treatment, Bid-/- mice show a significant increase in left internal ventricular diameter during diastole (LVIDd) compared to Bid+/+ mice.
claims.source: However, we find a significant increase in left internal ventricular diameter during diastole (LVIDd) (p<0.01) as well as during systole (LVIDs) (p<0.05) 18 hr after Epi (Figure 4c and d).
claims.evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4c.

claims.claim: 18 hours after acute Epinephrine treatment, Bid-/- mice show a significant increase in left internal ventricular diameter during systole (LVIDs) compared to Bid+/+ mice.
claims.source: However, we find a significant increase in left internal ventricular diameter during diastole (LVIDd) (p<0.01) as well as during systole (LVIDs) (p<0.05) 18 hr after Epi (Figure 4c and d).
claims.evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4d.

claims.claim: 18 hours after acute Epinephrine treatment, Bid-/- mice show a significant decrease in Ejection Fraction (EF) compared to Bid+/+ mice.
claims.source: This corresponds to a significant decrease in Ejection Fraction (EF) for Bid-/- mice (p<0.01) (Figure 4e)
claims.evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4e.

claims.claim: 18 hours after acute Epinephrine treatment, Bid-/- mice show an increase in both end diastolic and end systolic volume compared to Bid+/+ mice.
claims.source: Furthermore, we also observe an increase in both end diastolic (p<0.01) and end systolic volume (p<0.05) (Figure 4f and g) with stress.
claims.evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4f and g.

claims.claim: Decreased LV cardiac function observed in Bid-/- mice is phenotypically similar to observations made by echo in patients during the acute phase of MI.
claims.source: Decreased LV cardiac function observed in Bid-/- mice is phenotypically similar to observations made by echo in patients during the acute phase of MI (LV wall dilation and decreased ejection fraction) (White et al., 1987; Di Bella et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature describing MI phenotypes in humans.

claims.claim: At 5 days post-Epinephrine, both Bid+/+ and Bid-/- mice have restored cardiac function.
claims.source: Interestingly, at 5 days post-Epi, both the Bid+/+ and Bid-/- mice had restored cardiac function and we find no difference in heart weights at sacrifice (Figure 4c–g and Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4c-g.

claims.claim: Doxorubicin treatment results in a significant decrease in fractional shortening (FS) and ejection fraction (EF) in Bid-/- mice.
claims.source: Dox also resulted in a significant decrease in FS and EF (p<0.01) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c and d) in Bid-/- mice.
claims.evidence: This is supported by echocardiography data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c and d.

claims.claim: Using two different models (Epinephrine and Doxorubicin), Bid plays a role in maintaining LV function under stress.
claims.source: Thus, using two different models, Epinephrine, which directly results in increased oxygen demand, as well as the mitochondrial toxic drug Doxorubicin, we find that Bid plays a role in maintaining LV function under stress.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the echocardiography data showing decreased cardiac function in Bid-/- mice under both Epinephrine and Doxorubicin stress.

claims.claim: Myocardial fibrosis due to cardiomyocyte remodeling after damage is a prominent sequelae of MI and directly contributes to loss of cardiac function.
claims.source: Myocardial fibrosis due to cardiomyocyte remodeling after damage is a prominent sequelae of MI, and directly contributes to loss of cardiac function (Talman and Ruskoaho, 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: Bid-/- tissue has significantly increased fibrosis both at 18 hours and 5 days post Epinephrine treatment.
claims.source: We find that Bid-/- tissue has significantly increased fibrosis both at the 18 hr and the recovery time point, 5 days post treatment (p<0.05) (Figure 5b and c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Masson's trichrome staining and quantitation shown in Figure 5b and c.

claims.claim: WT mice display no increase in fibrosis at 18 hours post-Epinephrine; fibrosis develops in WT hearts at 5 days post-Epinephrine.
claims.source: Interestingly, WT mice display no increase in fibrosis at 18 hr post-Epi; fibrosis developed in WT hearts at 5 days post-Epi.
claims.evidence: This is supported by Masson's trichrome staining and quantitation shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Bid-/- mice have more fibrosis and increased susceptibility to damage after stress.
claims.source: Thus, Bid-/- mice have more fibrosis and increased susceptibility to damage after stress.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the fibrosis quantitation data.

claims.claim: Although Bid-/- mice are able to recover functionally after Epinephrine stress, the long-term damage is more severe.
claims.source: This result recapitulates the response to cardiomyocyte damage in human MI and suggests that although the Bid-/- mice are able to recover functionally, the long-term damage is more severe.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cardiac function recovers but fibrosis persists in Bid-/- mice.

claims.claim: MudPIT analysis identified 54 significantly different mitochondrial proteins between Bid+/+ and Bid-/- MPC samples.
claims.source: Cross referencing our hits to the Mouse MitoCarta 2.0 (Calvo et al., 2016), we identified 54 significantly different mitochondrial proteins between the Bid+/+ and Bid-/- samples (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b and c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by MudPIT proteomics data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Bid-/- heart mitochondria show a decrease in the activity of ATP synthase dimers.
claims.source: We observe a decrease in the activity of ATP synthase dimers from Bid-/- heart mitochondria (p<0.05) (Figure 6a and b)
claims.evidence: This is supported by in-gel activity assay data shown in Figure 6a and b.

claims.claim: The decrease in ATP synthase dimer activity is consistent with the known association between dimerization of ATP synthase in cristae loop formation and stabilization of cristae structure.
claims.source: We observe a decrease in the activity of ATP synthase dimers from Bid-/- heart mitochondria (p<0.05) (Figure 6a and b), consistent with the known association between dimerization of ATP synthase in cristae loop formation and stabilization of cristae structure (Hahn et al., 2016; Paumard et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Bid-/- heart mitochondria show a significant decrease in the activity of complex I within the supercomplexes.
claims.source: We observed a significant decrease in the activity of complex I within the SCs and a trend for decreased activity of complex IV containing SCs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1d,e and f).
claims.evidence: This is supported by in-gel activity assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1d, e, and f.

claims.claim: Bid-/- MPCs display significantly decreased oxygen consumption rates (OCR) compared to Bid+/+ cells.
claims.source: Using an Oroboros Oxygraph, we found Bid-/- MPCs displayed significantly decreased oxygen consumption rates (OCR) compared to Bid+/+ cells (p=0.008)
claims.evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 6c.

claims.claim: Respiration can be restored in Bid-/- MPCs by re-introduction of FHA-BidBH3.
claims.source: Respiration could be restored in Bid-/- MPCs by re-introduction of FHA-BidBH3 and FHA-BidD59A but not FHA-Bid into Bid-/- MPCs (Bid-/- v. Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3, p<0.0001 and Bid-/- v. FHA-BidD59A, p=0.0008) (Figure 6c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 6c.

claims.claim: Respiration can be restored in Bid-/- MPCs by re-introduction of FHA-BidD59A.
claims.source: Respiration could be restored in Bid-/- MPCs by re-introduction of FHA-BidBH3 and FHA-BidD59A but not FHA-Bid into Bid-/- MPCs (Bid-/- v. Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3, p<0.0001 and Bid-/- v. FHA-BidD59A, p=0.0008) (Figure 6c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 6c.

claims.claim: Baseline mitochondrial and cellular superoxide do not differ between Bid-/- and Bid +/+ MPCs.
claims.source: We assessed baseline mitochondrial and cellular superoxide with MitoSOX and DHE, respectively, and found no difference between Bid-/- and Bid +/+ MPCs
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2a and c.

claims.claim: Mitochondrial superoxide is increased in Bid-/- cells under conditions of nutrient withdrawal.
claims.source: however mitochondrial superoxide was increased in Bid-/- cells under conditions of nutrient withdrawal (p<0.01) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2a,b and c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2b.

claims.claim: Bid's phosphorylation sites S61 and S78 have been shown to correspond with increased ROS and respiration in hematopoietic stem cells.
claims.source: Bid's phosphorylation sites S61 and S78 (BidAA) have also been shown to correspond with increased ROS and respiration in hematopoietic stem cells (Maryanovich et al., 2012),(Maryanovich et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: FHA-BidBH3AA MPCs do not have altered membrane potential compared to BidBH3.
claims.source: We find that compared to BidBH3, FHA-BidBH3AA MPCs do not have altered membrane potential and show only a trend for increased ROS (p=0.1956) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2d and e).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TMRE staining data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2d.

claims.claim: The results in MPCs are most consistent with a role for S61 and S78 phosphorylation sites in overall cell viability by preventing caspase-8 cleavage of Bid, rather than specifically in the regulation of mitochondrial membrane potential or ROS production.
claims.source: Thus, our results in MPCs are most consistent with a role for these phosphorylation sites in overall cell viability, by preventing caspase-8 cleavage of Bid (Desagher et al., 2001), rather than specifically in the regulation of mitochondrial membrane potential or ROS production.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that BidBH3AA cells are unstable and do not show significant changes in membrane potential or ROS.

claims.claim: Bid-/- LV fibers display significantly decreased oxygen consumption compared to Bid+/+ LV fibers in state 3 respiration.
claims.source: Bid-/- LV fibers also displayed significantly decreased oxygen consumption compared to Bid+/+ LV fibers (p=0.0103) (Figure 6d).
claims.evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 6d.

claims.claim: Bid-/- permeabilized cardiac fibers have decreased respiratory function and decreased ATP production in the presence of complex I substrates.
claims.source: Bid-/- fibers had decreased respiratory function as well as decreased ATP production (p<0.05) (Figure 6e and f) compared to Bid +/+ fibers.
claims.evidence: This is supported by simultaneous ATP and O2 consumption measurements shown in Figure 6e and f.

claims.claim: Bid-/- permeabilized cardiac fibers have decreased respiration and decreased ATP production in the presence of rotenone and succinate.
claims.source: Bid-/- PmFBs had decreased respiration in the presence of rotenone and succinate (p<0.001), and decreased ATP production (p<0.05) (Figure 6e and f)
claims.evidence: This is supported by simultaneous ATP and O2 consumption measurements shown in Figure 6e and f.

claims.claim: Despite an overall decrease in respiration and ATP production, Bid-/- permeabilized cardiac fibers have similar oxidative phosphorylation efficiency to Bid +/+ when using complex I substrates.
claims.source: Interestingly, despite an overall decrease in respiration and ATP production, Bid-/- PmFBs have similar efficiency to Bid +/+ when using CI substrates.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ATP/O ratio calculations shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2f.

claims.claim: In the presence of rotenone and succinate, Bid-/- permeabilized cardiac fibers have an increased ATP/O ratio.
claims.source: However, in the presence of rotenone and succinate, Bid-/- PmFBs have an increased ATP/O ratio (p<0.05) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2f).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ATP/O ratio calculations shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2f.

claims.claim: Bid-/- mitochondria may compensate by bypassing complex I in favor of respiratory complex II, which is not found in respiratory supercomplexes and therefore would be less impacted by disorganized cristae.
claims.source: This suggests Bid-/- mitochondria may compensate by bypassing complex I in favor of respiratory complex I I, which is not found in respiratory supercomplexes (Schägger and Pfeiffer, 2001) and therefore would be less impacted by disorganized cristae.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the increased ATP/O ratio in the presence of rotenone and succinate, and supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Decreased BID expression is significantly associated with MI in BioVU.
claims.source: Consistent with our findings in mice, we observed that decreased BID expression is significantly associated with MI (Figure 7b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claims.claim: The BID heritability estimate is significant (h2 = 0.08 with standard error [SE] of 0.026).
claims.source: The BID heritability estimate was significant (h2 = 0.08 with standard error [SE] of 0.026), providing support for genetic regulation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a and b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by heritability analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b.

claims.claim: Individuals with the lowest 5% of BID expression have a > 4 fold increase in the prevalence of myocardial infarction compared to the rest of the Synthetic Derivative.
claims.source: Within this group, we find a > 4 fold increase in the prevalence of myocardial infarction compared to the rest of the Synthetic Derivative (Figure 7b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by analysis of BioVU data shown in Figure 7b.

claims.claim: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associates with myocardial infarction (p=7.55×10−3).
claims.source: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associated with myocardial infarction (p=7.55×10−3) as well as coronary atherosclerosis (p=8.26×10−3), and ischemic heart disease (p=9.7×10−4) (Figure 7b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claims.claim: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associates with coronary atherosclerosis (p=8.26×10−3).
claims.source: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associated with myocardial infarction (p=7.55×10−3) as well as coronary atherosclerosis (p=8.26×10−3), and ischemic heart disease (p=9.7×10−4) (Figure 7b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claims.claim: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associates with ischemic heart disease (p=9.7×10−4).
claims.source: Decreased BID expression in heart tissue significantly associated with myocardial infarction (p=7.55×10−3) as well as coronary atherosclerosis (p=8.26×10−3), and ischemic heart disease (p=9.7×10−4) (Figure 7b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claims.claim: There is no significant association between BID genetically determined expression and atrial fibrillation (p=0.63).
claims.source: Notably, we find no significant association between BID genetically determined expression and atrial fibrillation in this dataset (p=0.63), consistent with the lack of significant association in BioVU.
claims.evidence: This is supported by S-PrediXcan analysis of atrial fibrillation GWAS data.

claims.claim: BID's effect is specific to particular cardiac pathophysiologies.
claims.source: Thus, while we identify multiple cardiac traits associated with BID expression, BID's effect is specific to particular pathophysiologies.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that BID associates with MI but not atrial fibrillation.

claims.claim: A significant correlation (p=0.002) exists between decreased genetically determined BID expression in the aorta and MI in a separate BioVU sample set.
claims.source: In a separate BioVU sample set (see Materials and methods and Figure 7—figure supplement 1c and d), we observed a significant correlation (p=0.002) between decreased genetically determined BID expression in the aorta and MI.
claims.evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis in a validation cohort shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1c and d.

claims.claim: Decreased genetically determined expression of BID in heart is associated (p=0.02, effect size = −0.06, SE = 0.026) with MI in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D.
claims.source: Consistent with the BioVU discovery and validation results, decreased genetically determined expression of BID in heart was associated (p=0.02, effect size = −0.06, SE = 0.026) with MI in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D.
claims.evidence: This is supported by S-PrediXcan analysis of CARDIoGRAMplusC4D data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3a.

claims.claim: No association with MI in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D was observed with BCL2L13 (p=0.75).
claims.source: However, no association with MI in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D was observed with BCL2L13 (p=0.75) (Figure 7—figure supplement 3a and b), consistent with the SNPs being regulatory for BID.
claims.evidence: This is supported by S-PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3a.

claims.claim: A significant association was observed between carrier status for any missense variant in BID and MI (p=0.013; OR 1.7 [95% CI 1.1–2.6]).
claims.source: In multivariable logistic regression, a significant association was observed between carrier status (i.e. presence of any missense variant) and MI (p=0.013; OR 1.7 [95% CI 1.1–2.6]).
claims.evidence: This is supported by exome-chip analysis in BioVU shown in Figure 8b.

claims.claim: Carrier status for MBD variants is strongly associated with MI (p=0.002; OR 8.5 [95% CI 2.1–33.6]).
claims.source: Carrier status for MBD variants (i.e. presence of any missense variant in the MBD) was strongly associated with MI (p=0.002; OR 8.5 [95% CI 2.1–33.6]) (Figure 8b and c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by exome-chip analysis in BioVU shown in Figure 8b and c.

claims.claim: M148T was associated with MI risk (p=0.029, OR = 1.47) in a meta-analysis of exome-chip studies involving 42,335 patients and 78,240 controls of European ancestry.
claims.source: Notably, M148T was also associated with MI risk (p=0.029, OR = 1.47) in the recent meta-analysis of exome-chip studies involving 42,335 patients and 78,240 controls of European ancestry, consistent with the BioVU results (Stitziel et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a meta-analysis study.

claims.claim: The M148T mutation in BidBH3 fails to restore cristae structure in Bid-/- MPCs.
claims.source: We evaluated mitochondrial cristae number in Bid +/+, Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3 and Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3M148T (double mutant) as in Figure 2, and found that the double mutant had significantly less cristae compared to FHA-BidBH3 alone (p<0.01).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TEM and quantitation shown in Figure 8e, f, and g.

claims.claim: The BidBH3/M148T double mutant has an increase in overall mitochondrial area density per cell, likely as a compensatory mechanism for decreased cristae function.
claims.source: Interestingly, we found that the double mutant had an increase in overall mitochondrial area density per cell, likely as a compensatory mechanism for decreased cristae function (p<0.01) (Figure 8e–g).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitation shown in Figure 8g, with speculation about the mechanism.

claims.claim: Expression of the BidBH3/M148T double mutant is insufficient to restore respiratory levels comparable to Bid +/+ or Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3 MPCs.
claims.source: Expression of the BidBH3/M148T double mutant was insufficient to restore respiratory levels comparable to Bid +/+ or Bid-/- + FHA-BidBH3 MPCs (Figure 8h).
claims.evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 8h.

claims.claim: BidBH3/E120D MPCs have equivalent respiration compared to BH3-mutated Bid.
claims.source: Compared to BH3-mutated Bid, BidBH3/E120D MPCs had equivalent respiration.
claims.evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1d.

claims.claim: BidBH3/R124Q MPCs have decreased respiration compared to BH3-mutated Bid, but not significantly different from WT MPCs.
claims.source: While BidBH3/R124Q MPCs had decreased respiration (Figure 8—figure supplement 1d), it was not significantly different from WT MPCs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by respirometry data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1d.

claims.claim: Neither BidBH3/E120D nor BidBH3/R124Q MPCs display altered sensitivity to TNF-α/Actinomycin D stimulated cell death.
claims.source: Neither BidBH3/E120D nor BidBH3/R124Q MPCs displayed altered sensitivity to TNF-α/Actinomycin D stimulated cell death (Figure 8—figure supplement 1e and f).
claims.evidence: This is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1e and f.

claims.claim: Mcl-1 has a matrix isoform involved in respiratory chain maintenance and mitochondrial metabolism.
claims.source: In particular, the anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family member Mcl-1 has been shown to have a matrix isoform involved in respiratory chain maintenance and mitochondrial metabolism (Escudero et al., 2018; Perciavalle et al., 2012; Thomas et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: The BH3-domain of cBid associates with Mcl-1 to inhibit apoptosis.
claims.source: It is known that the BH3-domain of cBid associates with Mcl-1, to inhibit apoptosis (Clohessy et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: FlagHA-tagged Bid can immunoprecipitate WT Mcl-1, Mcl-1OM, and Mcl-1Matrix.
claims.source: Using FlagHA-tagged Bid expressed in 293 T cells, we were able to immunoprecipitate all three forms of Mcl-1 (Figure 9a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9a.

claims.claim: Bim does not associate with Mcl-1Matrix.
claims.source: This is in contrast to the other BH3-only protein Bim, which did not associate with Mcl-1Matrix (Perciavalle et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: FHA-BidM148T displays decreased association with Mcl-1Matrix compared to both WT-Bid and FHA-BidD59A.
claims.source: We find that FHA-BidM148T displays decreased association with Mcl-1Matrix compared to both WT-Bid and our rescue mutant, FHA-BidD59A.
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9b.

claims.claim: FHA-BidM148T displays increased association with WT Mcl-1 relative to either WT Bid or FHA-BidD59A.
claims.source: Furthermore, FHA-BidM148T displays increased association with WT Mcl-1 relative to either WT Bid or FHA-BidD59A (Figure 9b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9b.

claims.claim: The results are consistent with a role for helix-6 in Bid's association with Mcl-1Matrix in the context of the mitochondrial cristae.
claims.source: The above results are consistent with a role for helix-6 in Bid's association with Mcl-1Matrix, in the context of the mitochondrial cristae.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data showing differential binding of BidM148T to Mcl-1Matrix.

claims.claim: Loss of Mcl-1 has been shown to result in cardiomyopathy.
claims.source: Loss of Mcl-1 has previously been shown to result in cardiomyopathy (Wang et al., 2013) and impaired autophagy leading to heart failure in mice (Thomas et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Decreased genetically determined expression of MCL-1 is significantly associated with MI (p=0.00903).
claims.source: We find that decreased genetically determined expression of MCL-1 is significantly associated with MI (p=0.00903) (Figure 9c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 9c.

claims.claim: MTX1 has reduced genetically determined expression significantly associated with MI (p=1.93×10−5).
claims.source: In addition to MCL-1, we find that MTX1 (Metaxin1), a mitochondrial protein transporter that associates with the MICOS complex (Guarani et al., 2015), has reduced genetically determined expression significantly associated with MI (p=1.93×10−5).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PrediXcan analysis shown in Figure 9c.

claims.claim: Patients with a history of cardiomyopathy have a significantly increased relative risk for MI compared to known risk factors.
claims.source: Interestingly, we find that patients with a history of cardiomyopathy have a significantly increased relative risk for MI compared to the known risk factors, connecting these two phenotypes genetically (Figure 9d).
claims.evidence: This is supported by contingency table analysis shown in Figure 9d.

claims.claim: Bid may perform its role at the mitochondrial matrix through interaction with Mcl-1.
claims.source: Finally, we find an association between Bid and the matrix form of Mcl-1 mediated by the helix-6 residue M148, suggesting that Bid may perform its role at the mitochondrial matrix through interaction with Mcl-1.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data and the functional studies.

results.result: Loss of full-length Bid results in decreased cristae number in myeloid progenitor cells (MPCs), which can be rescued by BH3-domain or caspase-8 cleavage site mutants, demonstrating an apoptosis-independent role for Bid in cristae maintenance.
results.evaluation: Claims C23-C28 and C32 provide converging evidence from TEM imaging, quantitative stereology, and rescue experiments with apoptosis-deficient mutants (FHA-BidBH3 and FHA-BidD59A). The statistical significance (p<0.0001) and appropriate controls support the conclusion that Bid regulates cristae structure independently of its apoptotic function.

results.result: Full-length Bid localizes to mitochondria under non-apoptotic conditions and is found both at the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) and in the mitoplast fraction.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C38 are supported by multiple complementary fractionation approaches (subcellular fractionation, Percoll purification, Proteinase K protection, and mitoplast isolation). The convergence of these independent methods provides strong evidence for Bid's mitochondrial localization in the absence of apoptotic stimuli.

results.result: Bid-/- mice exhibit severe cardiac cristae defects at baseline that are exacerbated by acute epinephrine stress, with structural similarities to mitochondria observed after myocardial infarction.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C44 are supported by TEM imaging and quantitative analysis showing significantly increased cristae width in Bid-/- tissue (p<0.0001), which worsens after epinephrine treatment. The comparison to MI-induced damage is supported by citation to prior literature, though direct quantitative comparison would strengthen this claim.

results.result: Bid-/- mice show normal cardiac function at baseline but develop significant cardiac dysfunction 18 hours after acute epinephrine stress, with increased ventricular diameters and decreased ejection fraction, followed by functional recovery at 5 days.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C51 are supported by echocardiography data with appropriate statistical analysis (p<0.01 for LVIDd, p<0.05 for LVIDs, p<0.01 for EF). The temporal progression and recovery are well-documented. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=12 baseline, n=10-12 at 18hr, n=5-6 at recovery), though one outlier was excluded.

results.result: Doxorubicin treatment also results in decreased cardiac function in Bid-/- mice, confirming Bid's role in maintaining cardiac function under multiple types of stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C53 are supported by echocardiography data (p<0.01 for FS and EF) using an independent stress model. However, the sample size is small (n=4 per group), which limits the strength of this conclusion. This result serves as important validation of the epinephrine findings.

results.result: Bid-/- mice exhibit significantly increased myocardial fibrosis both at 18 hours and 5 days post-epinephrine treatment, with earlier onset compared to wild-type mice, suggesting more severe long-term damage despite functional recovery.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C58 are supported by Masson's trichrome staining and quantitative analysis (p<0.05). The temporal pattern showing early fibrosis in Bid-/- mice (18hr) versus delayed fibrosis in WT mice (5 days) is well-documented. The interpretation of long-term damage is reasonable given the persistent fibrosis despite functional recovery.

results.result: Loss of Bid results in altered mitochondrial protein composition and decreased activity of ATP synthase dimers and respiratory complex I in heart mitochondria.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C62 are supported by MudPIT proteomics identifying 54 significantly different mitochondrial proteins and in-gel activity assays showing decreased ATP synthase dimer activity (p<0.05) and complex I activity. The connection to cristae structure is supported by citations to prior literature. Sample sizes for activity assays are adequate (n=3-4).

results.result: Bid-/- MPCs display significantly decreased oxygen consumption that can be rescued by re-introduction of BH3-mutated or D59A-mutated Bid but not wild-type Bid.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C65 are supported by Oroboros respirometry data with strong statistical significance (p=0.008 for Bid-/- vs WT; p<0.0001 for rescue with BidBH3; p=0.0008 for rescue with BidD59A). The failure of WT Bid to rescue is explained by production of cleaved Bid (C31), which is consistent with the apoptosis-independent function.

results.result: Bid-/- cardiac fibers exhibit decreased oxygen consumption and ATP production with both complex I and complex II substrates, but maintain similar oxidative phosphorylation efficiency with complex I substrates and show increased ATP/O ratio with complex II substrates, suggesting compensatory mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C76 are supported by simultaneous ATP and O2 consumption measurements in permeabilized cardiac fibers with appropriate statistical analysis. The interpretation of compensatory complex II usage (C76) is reasonable given the increased ATP/O ratio with rotenone/succinate, though this remains somewhat speculative. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=3-6).

results.result: Decreased genetically determined BID expression is significantly associated with myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis, and ischemic heart disease in BioVU, with patients in the lowest 5% of BID expression showing >4-fold increased MI risk, and this association is specific to particular cardiac pathophysiologies (not atrial fibrillation).
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C84 are supported by PrediXcan analysis in a large cohort (29,366 patients) with significant p-values (p=7.55×10⁻³ for MI, p=8.26×10⁻³ for coronary atherosclerosis, p=9.7×10⁻⁴ for ischemic heart disease). The heritability estimate is significant (h²=0.08, SE=0.026). The >4-fold increased MI risk in the lowest 5% of expression is striking. The specificity is supported by lack of association with atrial fibrillation (p=0.63).

results.result: The association between decreased BID expression and MI is validated in an independent BioVU cohort and in the CARDIoGRAMplusC4D GWAS dataset, with evidence that SNPs are regulatory for BID rather than the adjacent BCL2L13 gene.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C87 provide independent validation in separate cohorts. The BioVU validation shows p=0.002 for aorta expression, and CARDIoGRAMplusC4D shows p=0.02 for heart expression. The lack of association with BCL2L13 (p=0.75) supports the specificity for BID. The effect size in CARDIoGRAMplusC4D is modest (−0.06) but consistent with the discovery cohort.

results.result: Carrier status for missense variants in BID, particularly in the membrane binding domain (MBD), is strongly associated with MI risk, with the M148T variant showing association in both BioVU and a large meta-analysis.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C90 are supported by exome-chip analysis showing significant associations (p=0.013 for any BID variant, OR=1.7; p=0.002 for MBD variants, OR=8.5). The M148T association is validated in an independent meta-analysis (p=0.029, OR=1.47). However, the very high OR for MBD variants (8.5) should be interpreted cautiously given the rarity of these variants and potential for winner's curse.

results.result: The M148T mutation in BH3-mutated Bid fails to restore cristae structure and respiratory function in Bid-/- MPCs, with compensatory increase in mitochondrial density.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C93 are supported by TEM quantitation showing significantly fewer cristae in the BidBH3/M148T double mutant compared to BidBH3 alone (p<0.01), increased mitochondrial density (p<0.01), and failure to restore respiration. The compensatory mechanism interpretation (C92) is speculative but reasonable. This directly links the human genetic variant to mitochondrial function.

results.result: Other MBD variants (E120D and R124Q) show different functional effects, with E120D maintaining normal respiration and R124Q showing intermediate effects, and neither affecting apoptotic sensitivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C96 are supported by respirometry and viability assays. The differential effects of these variants provide important specificity for the M148T finding. However, the lack of significant difference between R124Q and WT (C95) makes interpretation of this variant uncertain. The preservation of apoptotic function is important for demonstrating specificity.

results.result: Full-length Bid associates with all three forms of Mcl-1 (WT, OM, and Matrix), but the M148T mutation decreases association with Mcl-1Matrix while increasing association with WT Mcl-1, suggesting a role for helix-6 in Mcl-1Matrix interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C103 are supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments in 293T cells. The differential binding of BidM148T to different Mcl-1 isoforms is clearly demonstrated. However, the experiments are performed in an overexpression system, which may not fully recapitulate endogenous interactions. The interpretation regarding helix-6's role (C103) is reasonable but somewhat speculative.

results.result: Decreased genetically determined expression of MCL-1 and MTX1 (genes involved in cristae regulation) is significantly associated with MI, and patients with cardiomyopathy have significantly increased relative risk for MI.
results.evaluation: Claims C105-C107 are supported by PrediXcan analysis showing significant associations (p=0.00903 for MCL-1, p=1.93×10⁻⁵ for MTX1) and contingency table analysis for cardiomyopathy. This provides important convergent evidence linking cristae regulation to MI risk. However, the connection between cardiomyopathy and MI could have confounding factors not fully addressed.

results.result: Baseline mitochondrial and cellular superoxide do not differ between Bid-/- and Bid+/+ MPCs, but mitochondrial superoxide is increased in Bid-/- cells under nutrient withdrawal.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C67 are supported by flow cytometry with MitoSOX and DHE. The lack of baseline ROS differences is important for ruling out oxidative damage as the primary mechanism. The increased ROS under stress (p<0.01) suggests Bid-/- cells are more vulnerable to metabolic stress, consistent with the overall findings.

results.result: Bid's phosphorylation sites S61 and S78 do not significantly alter mitochondrial membrane potential or ROS production in MPCs, suggesting their role is primarily in preventing caspase-8 cleavage rather than directly regulating mitochondrial function.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C70 are based on experiments with BidBH3AA mutant, but the authors note these cells were highly unstable, which limits interpretation. The lack of significant changes in membrane potential and only a trend for increased ROS (p=0.1956) is reported, but the instability of the cell line raises questions about whether the experiments adequately test the hypothesis. The interpretation (C70) is reasonable but speculative.

results.result: Loss of Bid does not lead to compensatory upregulation of other BH3-only proteins (Bim, Bad, Puma) in MPCs or cardiac tissue.
results.evaluation: Claim C33 is supported by Western blot analysis in both MPCs and LV cardiac tissue. This is an important control to rule out compensatory mechanisms by other BH3-only proteins. However, the analysis is limited to protein levels and does not assess potential changes in activity or localization of these proteins.

results.result: Bid-/- cells have slightly decreased mitochondrial density, while FHA-BidD59A expressing cells have increased mitochondrial density compared to all other cell lines.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C30 are supported by quantitative TEM analysis (p<0.05 for Bid-/- decrease). The increased density in BidD59A cells is interesting but the mechanism is unclear. This could represent a compensatory response or an artifact of the rescue construct. The biological significance of these changes in density is uncertain.

results.result: Overexpression of full-length WT Bid but not FHA-BidBH3 or FHA-BidD59A results in production of endogenous cleaved Bid in the absence of a death stimulus.
results.evaluation: Claim C31 is supported by Western blot data showing cleaved Bid in cells expressing WT Bid but not in cells expressing the mutants. This explains why WT Bid fails to rescue the phenotype and supports the apoptosis-independent function of full-length Bid. The observation is important for interpreting the rescue experiments.
